newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian anger flares over Israeli policy.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian anger flares over Israeli policy.

text.p: A senior official close to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Sunday the time for passive resistance to Israel's settlement policy was over.

"The danger surrounding us is forcing us to decide whether to be free and masters over our land or slaves of the Israelis," Ahmed Abdel Rahman, general-secretary of Arafat's cabinet, said in a fiery speech in self-ruled Gaza.

"From now on, resisting settlements will not be through words, condemnation or complaints to the U.N. Security Council," he told a rally organised by the Islamic National Committee to Resist Settlements and the Palestinian Information Ministry.
Arafat condemned on Saturday a U.S. veto of a U.N. Security Council resolution calling on Israel to abandon plans to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in mainly Arab East Jerusalem.

Introduced at the rally as speaking on Arafat's behalf, Abdel Rahman said: "The world is with you but the world will not carry a rock for you." Stone-throwing was the hallmark of the 1987-1993 Palestinian uprising in the West Bank and Gaza.

"Jerusalem is a burning object that will ignite this hopeless peace. We have been patient for so long but today the knife is at our necks," Abdel Rahman told the gathering attended by several hundred Palestinians.

Nahed al-Rayes, a leader of Arafat's Fatah faction in the Palestine Liberation Organisation and a supporter of the peace process with Israel, said he now owed an apology to those who opposed the deals with the Jewish state.

"The principle of compromise which the Palestinian people accepted...has been violated by the Israelis and the Americans and now everything is back at the starting point, at ground zero," he told the rally.

The militant Islamic Resistance Group Hamas called on Palestinians to confront settlements by "all means". Hamas, which rejected the PLO accords with Israel, spearheaded a wave of suicide bombings in Israel last year that killed 59 people,
"We call on all Palestinian factions to work towards a complete resistance agenda to confront settlement and to recruit the masses and all means," Hamas said in a statement.

Palestinians were also angry over Israel's decision on Friday to pull out of nine percent of the West Bank in the first of three troop redeployments due to be completed by mid-1998 under a peace deal.
PLO officials said they had expected 30 percent of the land to be handed over, although the U.S.-brokered deal left it up to Israel to determine the scope of the pullback.
"We reject the false redeployment announced by the Israeli government," said another speaker at the rally, Isam Abdel al-Latif, a member of the settlement resistance committee.
The committee's East Jerusalem office is one of four Palestinian institutions warned last week by Israeli police to shut voluntarily or be closed down.

A 96-hour warning period before police could issue closure orders expired on Sunday. But Israel's Public Security Ministry said police would take no action until they met later in the day with a Palestinian lawyer challenging the orders.
Israel has charged the offices act illegally on behalf of the Palestinian Authority, which is barred by the peace deals from operating in Jerusalem.

The PLO wants East Jerusalem as the capital of a Palestinian state. Israel sees all the city as its indivisible capital. Jerusalem's final status is to be negotiated in Israel-PLO talks due to start later in the month.
